newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Simsmetal sees better second half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Simsmetal sees better second half.

text.p: Metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Tuesday it expects an improvement in profitability in the second half of the financial year to June 30 due to a general improvement in demand for secondary ferrous and non-ferrous metals.

"There has been a general improvement in demand and prices for both secondary ferrous and non-ferrous metals in recent weeks, and if these increases are sustained, this will assist second half results," managing director John Crabb said.
"Accordingly the group is forecasting an improvement in profitability in the second half of financial year 1997," Crabb said in a statement.
Simsmetal earlier reported a 42.9 percent fall in net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 to A$14.07 million.
Crabb said first half earnings in Simsmetal's Australian and overseas operations were hit by lower demand and lower prices for both secondary ferrous and non ferrous metals.

The ferrous division in particular experienced intense margin pressure in the second quarter, Crabb said. "The strength of the Australian dollar and lower volumes in most regions, compared to the first half of the previous financial year, were also significant factors in the downturn," he said.
The contribution from the non-ferrous division improved in the second quarter as prices strengthened, while the aluminium division also picked up in the second quarter.
Simsmetal said in November that the poor outlook for metal prices meant profit for the year to June 30, 1997 would be lower than in 1995/96.
Crabb said on Tuesday that Consolidated Extrusions, a joint venture with G.E. Crane Holdings Ltd, showed improved earnings in the second quarter.

Simsmetal had completed the purchase of half of Richmond Steel Recycling Ltd in Canada in December 1996 and would commission new shredding plants. It would also launch a self-sevice auto parts business near Sydney in February.
